title: Digging into the Chemical Complexity in the Outer Galaxy: A Hot Molecular Core in Sh 2-283
question: What is the chemical complexity of the outer Galactic hot core Sh 2-283-1a SMM1, and how do its molecular abundances compare to hot cores in the inner Galaxy, outer Galaxy, and Magellanic Clouds to constrain the role of environmental factors beyond metallicity?

data.sensitivity: 0.02–0.03 K per channel in extracted spectrum

what.value: Distance and galactocentric distance to Sh 2-283 based on Gaia EDR3 astrometry of ALS 18674

evidence.quote: According to the astrometric data of a nearby cluster member (ALS 18674) in the Gaia Early Data Release 3 (cite: Gaia2021; Bra19), the distance to the Sh 2-283 region is estimated to be 7.9$^{+1.2}_{-1.1}$ kpc, which corresponds to the galactocentric distance of 15.7$^{+1.1}_{-0.9}$ kpc (cite: Ikeda2025).

what.value: Metallicity of Sh 2-283 (~0.3 Z_sun) from optical spectroscopy of associated H II region

evidence.quote: The metallicity of this region is estimated to be approximately 30$\%$ of the solar value based on optical spectroscopy of the associated H$_\mathrm{II}$ region (cite: Fer17).

what.value: Mass absorption coefficient of dust grains coated by thin ice mantles (1.89 cm^2 g^-1 at 870 um)

evidence.quote: $\kappa_{\nu}$ is the mass absorption coefficient of dust grains coated by thin ice mantles taken from (cite: Oss94) and we use 1.89 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 870 $\mu$m.

To avoid this underestimation, we estimated $N$(CH$_3$OH) from the $^{13}$CH$_3$OH column density, assuming a $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 100 based on the isotope ratio gradients reported by (cite: Milam2005) and (cite: Yan2023) at $D_{\mathrm{GC}}$ = 15.7 kpc.

evidence.loc: Molecular abundances: Comparison with the Galactic and Magellanic hot cores
evidence.quote: The CH$_3$OH and SO$_2$ column densities for the inner Galactic sources were taken from (cite: Fuente2014; Gelder2022L; Qin2022; Li2025) and (cite: Fuente2014; Santos2024).

evidence.quote: We calculated the H$_2$ column densities for the sources in (cite: Santos2024) by using the continuum data summarized in (cite: Gelder2022L), following the method used in Section 3.4.

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration followed by one round of continuum phase self-calibration, visibility continuum subtraction, Briggs-weighted cleaning, and primary beam correction
assumptions: 10% systematic uncertainty on absolute flux scale

recipe.goal: Extract spectrum, identify molecular lines, and fit line profiles
recipe.method: Extract spectrum from an elliptical aperture at the continuum/CH3OH peak, identify transitions using CDMS and JPL databases, smooth or bin weak lines, and fit Gaussian profiles to measure line parameters
key_parameters: Elliptical extraction aperture: 0.89'' x 0.70'' centered at RA = 6h38m29.660s, Dec = 0d44m40.75s
Detection criteria: >= 3 sigma and within ~+-2 km s^-1 of V_sys = 53.2 km s^-1 (2.5–3 sigma with spatial coincidence for tentative detections)
Savitzky-Golay filter: window size = 5 channels, polynomial order = 3; or 2-channel binning

recipe.method: Integrate spectral cubes over visually inspected velocity ranges (~+-FWHM) and stack multiple transitions for selected species to reduce noise
key_parameters: Velocity integration range: typically ~+-FWHM determined by visual inspection

recipe.goal: Derive rotational temperatures and molecular column densities
recipe.method: Rotational diagram analysis under optically thin LTE for SO2, CH3OH, and CH2DOH; fixed rotational temperatures (50 K or 150 K) for species with 1–2 lines; optical depth correction for CH3OH by scaling 13CH3OH with 12C/13C = 100
key_parameters: SO2 separated into two components: E_u < 100 K and E_u >= 100 K; blended SO2(13_{2,12}–12_{1,11}) excluded
Fixed T_rot = 50 K (cold component) and 150 K (warm component)
assumptions: Optically thin emission and Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE)

recipe.goal: Estimate H2 column density, gas volume density, and fractional abundances
recipe.method: Calculate N(H2) from optically thin 0.87 mm dust continuum emission, divide by core extent to get gas volume density, and compute N(X)/N(H2) and N(X)/N(CH3OH) ratios
key_parameters: kappa_nu = 1.89 cm^2 g^-1 at 870 um (thin ice mantles), dust-to-gas mass ratio Z = 0.0024, T_d = 150 K (range 80–180 K), core extent = 6.5 x 10^3 au
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission at 870 um, dust coated by thin ice mantles, T_d = 150 K, and Z = 0.0024

evidence.quote: Spectral lines were identified by determining the systemic velocity ($V_\mathrm{{sys}}$) as 53.2 km s$^{-1}$ from the CH$_3$OH (5$_{4}$ A$^-$–6$_{3}$ A$^-$) line
The typical measured line widths are 3–6 km s$^{-1}$.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we adopt $N_{\rm{H_2}}$ = 1.4$^{+ 1.3}_{-0.3}$ $\times$ 10$^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$ as the representative value of H$_2$ column density.
The gas density of the core was estimated by dividing the $N_{\rm{H_2}}$ by its extent (6.5 $\times$ 10$^3$ au is assumed), and the derived value is 3.7 $\times$ 10$^6$ cm$^{-3}$.
The $N$(CH$_2$DOH)/$N$(CH$_3$OH) ratio of Sh 2-283-1a SMM1 is 1.5$^{+3.9}_{-1.2}$$\%$, comparable to that of inner Galactic high-mass sources.
The $N$(CH$_2$DOH)/$N$(CH$_3$OH) ratio of Sh 2-283-1a SMM1 is 1.5$^{+3.9}_{-1.2}$$\%$, which is comparable to that of the other outer Galactic hot core (cite: Shimonishi2021).
